The Story of Gajkumar Muni

I bow to Lord Jina, who became famous through his virtues and, having done all that needed to be done, has attained perfection and fulfilment, and I write the story of Gajkumar Muni.

Gajkumar was born to Vasudev's queen Gandharvasena in sacred Dwaraka, made pure by the birth of Lord Neminath. Gajkumar was a great warrior. The mere fame of his valour would burn away the vast creeper of his enemies' pride.

At that time, King Aparajit of Podanpur had caused great trouble. Vasudev tried many means to bring him under control, but by no means could he be captured. Then Vasudev had a proclamation made in the city: "Whoever brings my enemy Aparajit and presents him before me shall receive whatever boon he desires."

Hearing the proclamation, Gajkumar went to his father and, with joined hands, requested permission to lead the campaign against Aparajit himself. His request was granted. He marched with his army against Aparajit. A fierce battle ensued on both sides. In the end, the goddess of victory favoured Gajkumar. He captured Aparajit and presented him before his father. Vasudev was greatly pleased by Gajkumar's valour. He granted him whatever boon he desired.

Very few noble men, having received a boon, remain virtuous and contented. Gajkumar too fell from the path. Having received his father's boon, he turned toward injustice. The sinful prince began forcibly dishonouring the chaste wives of good families. He was a prince — who could stop him? And whoever dared to oppose him became a thorn in his eye, and Gajkumar would try to uproot them entirely. Cursed be that conduct which strips even fools of shame and fear.

In this way, Gajkumar dishonoured many noble women. But through fear of his power, no one dared speak. One day, he cast his eye upon Surti, the wife of merchant Pansul, and violated her. Seeing this, Pansul's heart burned with the fire of anger. But the poor man could do nothing. He had to sit silently at home.

One day, by the merit of worthy souls, Lord Neminath came to Dwaraka. Balbhadra, Vasudev, and others went to pay their respects. Gajkumar too went. Seeing the Lord's divine form, Gajkumar's heart was transformed. The Lord's discourse pierced his soul like an arrow. He realised the gravity of his sins and the impermanence of worldly power and pleasure. Overcome with repentance, he renounced everything, took initiation as a monk, and practised intense austerities.

Through dedicated spiritual practice, Gajkumar destroyed his karmas and attained omniscience. He became worthy of worship by the world and ultimately attained liberation.

This story teaches that no matter how deeply one has fallen into sin, the grace of the Lord and the power of dharma can transform even the worst sinner. Gajkumar, who had committed terrible crimes, through sincere repentance and dedicated practice, rose to the highest spiritual state. The wise should never despair of redemption.
